newsitem.title: UK: European VGO largely unchanged but arb said closed.
newsitem.headline: European VGO largely unchanged but arb said closed.

text.p: European vacuum gas oil prices were unchanged to a shade higher by mid-week, with low avails giving some support but a closed transatlantic arb putting a bit of pressure on the market.
Traders said a Scandinavian refiner sold earlier this week 25,000 tonnes of low sulphur VGO at about $123/$124, some $1 to $2 lower than its asking price by the end of last week.
Some traders said that cargo went into the barge market, which was valued at around the $133/$134 fob mark.

"At that price it is worthwhile for someone to take the material and actually ship it across there, put it in a tank and selling in the barge market compared to cargoes which are sort of $125ish," one trader said.
Some traders said market players were still looking to see if the arb to the United States was still workable while others said it was closed at the moment.
"Supplies are tight but the arb is definitely closed to the States now. They just don't want it (VGO) there at the moment, with the discounts widened again," a trader said.

One seller said he would have high sulphur cargoes soon and would be offering at about the $115/$116 mark, but added that buyers "were looking at the arb to the States. There's a little bit of hesitation".
